name: HVAC / Heating & Cooling
extra_prompt: You are booking for a heating and cooling company. Ask the brand and model if known, the system type (split, ducted, evaporative, heat pump, or gas heater), and its approximate age. Ask whether the unit runs at all and whether it blows warm or cold air. For gas heaters, a gas smell, a yellow or orange flame, or a carbon monoxide alarm is an emergency: tell the caller to turn the heater off, open windows, and get everyone outside, then treat it as an emergency. For installs, offer an on-site assessment before quoting.

kb.q: Do you do emergency AC repair?
kb.a: Yes, we run an emergency line for no-cool and no-heat calls. Availability depends on the season.

kb.q: Do you install new systems?
kb.a: Yes, we install and replace split systems, ducted systems, and heat pumps. Every install includes a load calculation and commissioning report.

kb.q: How much does a new AC unit cost?
kb.a: {price_note} Costs depend on the system type, the size needed, and how complex the install is. We give you a fixed quote after a site visit.

kb.q: Do you service commercial HVAC?
kb.a: Yes, we service light commercial systems, including rooftop units and split systems.

kb.q: What brands do you work on?
kb.a: All major brands — Daikin, Mitsubishi, Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Rheem, Goodman, and more.

kb.q: How long does a service call take?
kb.a: A standard AC service is one to two hours. Diagnostics can take longer if it is a complex fault.

kb.q: Do you offer financing?
kb.a: Yes, we offer financing on system replacements. Ask for details when we quote.

kb.q: Why is my AC leaking water?
kb.a: Usually a blocked condensate drain. It is a common issue and we can usually clear it in a single visit.

kb.q: My system is frozen — what should I do?
kb.a: Turn the system off at the thermostat immediately. Running a frozen system can damage the compressor. We can be out to diagnose the cause.

kb.q: How often should I change my filter?
kb.a: Every one to three months for standard filters. High-efficiency or heavily used systems need more frequent changes.

kb.q: Do you provide a warranty on repairs?
kb.a: {warranty_note}

kb.q: Can you install a smart thermostat?
kb.a: Yes, we install and configure all major smart thermostats including Nest, Ecobee, and Honeywell Home.

kb.q: Do you test for carbon monoxide?
kb.a: Yes, our heating service includes a carbon monoxide safety check. If you suspect a CO issue now, leave the property and call emergency services.

kb.q: How long does a new system install take?
kb.a: Most residential replacements take a full day. Ducted or commercial systems can take two or more days.

kb.q: Do you offer maintenance plans?
kb.a: Yes, our annual maintenance plan includes two services a year and priority booking for emergencies.

kb.q: What SEER rating should I choose?
kb.a: Higher SEER means lower running costs but higher upfront cost. We help match the right rating to your climate and usage.

kb.q: Can you repair a unit over twenty years old?
kb.a: We can, but on very old equipment we weigh repair cost against replacement and will always give you both options.

kb.q: How often should I service my air conditioner?
kb.a: Once a year is recommended for most systems, and before the start of summer or winter. Regular service keeps the efficiency up and prevents breakdowns.

kb.q: Is it worth repairing an old system?
kb.a: Often a repair is worth it on a system under about ten years old. For older systems, we give you a repair cost against a replacement cost so you can decide.

kb.q: Why does my air conditioner smell musty?
kb.a: A musty smell is usually mould or bacteria on the evaporator coil or in the drain pan. A clean and sanitise fixes most cases.

kb.q: Why is water dripping inside from my indoor unit?
kb.a: The condensate drain is usually blocked or the unit is not level. Switch the unit off and book a service so the drain can be cleared and checked.

kb.q: What size system do I need?
kb.a: It depends on room size, insulation, sun exposure and ceiling height. We do a load calculation on site and recommend a size that is neither too large nor too small.

kb.q: Do you offer a maintenance plan for heating and cooling?
kb.a: Yes. Our plans include a yearly or twice-yearly service, priority booking, and a discount on repairs.

kb.q: How often should I service my AC?
kb.a: Once a year before summer. A yearly service keeps efficiency high and catches small problems before they become expensive.
